title: U.S. adults 65+ set to outnumber children by 2029
excerpt: The U.S. Census Bureau projects adults 65 and older will outnumber children under 18 around 2029 — a first in U.S. history. See the chart and download the data.
content_html:
For most of recorded U.S. history, children have far outnumbered older adults. The U.S. Census Bureau now projects that this will reverse around 2029, when, for the first time, there will be more Americans aged 65 and older than children under 18.

The shift is not a forecast about a distant century. In 1950 there were almost four children for every older adult. By 2024 the two groups were about 12 million apart and closing. The latest official projection puts the crossover at the end of this decade. This page documents the convergence using the Bureau’s own counts and projections, with the full dataset available to download.

TL;DR — The number of U.S. adults 65+ has risen roughly five-fold since 1950 (12.3 million to 61.2 million), while the number of children under 18 has stayed near 73 million. On the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2023 projections (middle series), older adults overtake children around 2029 — the first such crossover in U.S. history, and earlier than the 2034 date in the Bureau’s superseded 2017 projections. Eleven states and nearly half of all U.S. counties have already crossed that line.

The two lines on the chart move for different reasons. The number of older Americans has risen almost without interruption: from 12.3 million in 1950 to 16.7 million in 1960, 25.5 million in 1980, 40.3 million in 2010, and 61.2 million by 2024. As a share of the population, the 65-and-older group grew from 8.1% in 1950 to 18.0% in 2024. The single fastest decade was 2010 to 2020, when the older population grew 38.6% — the fastest rate the Census Bureau records since the 1880s — as the first members of the baby-boom generation (born 1946–1964) began turning 65 in 2011.

The number of children has followed a flatter, wavier path. It climbed during the baby boom to about 69.8 million in 1970, dipped through the 1980s, recovered to about 74.2 million by 2010 — around its peak — and has since edged down to 73.1 million in 2024. But because the total population kept growing, the share of children declined over the long run — from a baby-boom peak of 36.0% in 1960 to 21.5% in 2024 (it was 31.3% in 1950, before the boom). The result is the long narrowing visible in the chart: a gap approaching 50 million in favour of children around 1970, down to about 12 million by 2024.

Between the 2020 census and the 2024 estimate, the mechanics are stark: the number of older adults rose from 55.8 million to 61.2 million — an increase of 5.4 million — while the number of children held essentially flat near 73 million. The entire closing of the gap over those four years came from the top line rising, not the bottom line falling.

The crossover, and why the date moved

The exact year of the crossover depends on which projection is used, and this is worth stating precisely because the widely-quoted figure has changed. The Census Bureau’s 2017 National Population Projections placed the crossover at 2034. Those projections have since been superseded by the Bureau’s 2023 National Population Projections — the first set built on the 2020 census and incorporating post-pandemic fertility and mortality. In the 2023 middle series, the older population overtakes the younger around 2029, five years earlier than the prior estimate. The shift reflects lower projected fertility pulling the under-18 line down faster than the 2017 series assumed.

The bracketing figures make the timing concrete. In the 2023 projection, children still lead in 2025 (about 70.9 million under 18 versus 63.3 million aged 65+). By 2030 the order has reversed (about 71.2 million aged 65+ versus 69.1 million under 18). The lines cross in between — in 2029. The earlier date is also more consistent with what has actually been observed: the gap closed from about 17 million in 2020 to about 12 million in 2024, a pace that points to the end of this decade rather than the middle of the 2030s.

This is not, in fact, a frontier the whole country reaches at once. As of 2024, eleven states and nearly half of all U.S. counties already had more residents aged 65 and older than children under 18. The national crossover near 2029 is the point at which the rest of the country, on aggregate, catches up to where many states and counties already are.

Three forces drive the convergence, and none of them is sudden. The baby-boom cohort is moving through the older age brackets in a single wave — every member of that generation is projected to be 65 or older by 2030. Life expectancy at older ages has risen over the long run, so each cohort lingers longer in the 65-plus group. And fertility has run below the replacement rate of about 2.1 children per woman for years (around 1.6 recently), which holds the under-18 line down. Looking further out, the Bureau’s middle series puts the 65-and-older share at 24.4% by 2060 and 29.1% by 2100, against 17.7% and 16.4% for children.

Two ways to read the same chart

The crossover is a single demographic fact, but it supports more than one interpretation, and the data does not settle which is right.

Some read this as a slow-moving fiscal pressure. Programs for older Americans — Social Security and Medicare in particular — are funded largely by working-age contributions. As the ratio of working-age adults (18–64) to older adults falls from about 3.4 today toward roughly 2.4 by 2060, the arithmetic that supports those programs tightens, all else equal. On this reading, the chart is an argument for some combination of higher productivity, longer working lives, higher fertility, or higher immigration to widen the working-age base.

Others read this as a marker of success rather than a problem. A growing older population is, in large part, the result of people living longer — a public-health achievement, not a failure. On this reading, the United States is also far from an outlier: in 2020 it ranked 34th among countries by the share of residents aged 65 and over, behind Japan (28.5%) and much of Europe, all of which remain high-income economies. The U.S. is aging later and more slowly than most of its peers, and an older age structure is something many wealthy societies already manage.

The chart shows the when and the structure of the shift. It does not show which policy response is correct, or whether the trajectory is a concern at all — that depends on assumptions the data alone cannot supply. Is the U.S. path more like Japan’s — older, slower-growing, and still high-income — or a manageable mid-century adjustment? The same chart is read both ways.

Counter-arguments and limitations

The crossover year is a projection, not an observation. Children still outnumber older adults today. The 2029 date comes from the Census Bureau’s 2023 middle series, one of several scenarios. Higher immigration would widen the working-age and child base and could push the crossover later; lower immigration or fertility would pull it earlier. The Bureau itself publishes high-, low-, and zero-immigration variants alongside the middle series for exactly this reason.

Counts and shares can tell slightly different stories. This page plots counts in millions, because the milestone — “more older adults than children” — is a statement about numbers of people. The crossover appears at the same point if the two groups are measured as a share of the population, since they share the same denominator. But share-based and count-based framings of “how much the country is aging” can diverge, and both are included in the downloadable dataset.

Age thresholds are conventions. “65 and older” and “under 18” are administratively meaningful (retirement eligibility, school age) but arbitrary as biological or economic categories. A 67-year-old in the labour force and a 17-year-old earner sit on the “wrong” side of those lines. The crossover is robust to small changes in the thresholds, but the precise gap is sensitive to where they are drawn.

The drivers are not equally certain. The baby-boom cohort’s path through the older brackets is close to fixed — those people are already alive and counted. Future fertility and immigration are far less predictable, and they are what determine how far past the crossover the gap eventually widens.

Common misinterpretations

Reading the crossover as already having happened nationally. It has not. As of the 2024 estimate, children still outnumber older adults in the country as a whole (73.1 million versus 61.2 million). The crossover is projected, not realised — even though it has already occurred in eleven states and nearly half of U.S. counties.

Treating 2029 and 2034 as competing facts. They are not contradictory; 2034 is simply the older estimate. The 2017 projections placed the crossover at 2034; the 2023 projections, which supersede them, place it at 2029. Citing 2034 today means citing a figure the Bureau has replaced.

Equating “more old people” with “fewer working-age people.” The working-age population (18–64) is projected to keep growing into the 2050s and then hold roughly level in the middle series — not to contract. What falls is the ratio of working-age adults to older adults. The pressure is relative, not a literal contraction of the workforce.

Reading the chart as a forecast of decline. The total U.S. population is projected to keep growing for decades, peaking near 370 million around 2080 in the middle series. The crossover is a change in the population’s age structure, not in its size.

Methodology and Sources

The middle series places the 65-plus/under-18 crossover at 2029; the superseded 2017 series placed it at 2034. The dotted lines are anchored to the 2024 estimate and drawn through the Bureau’s projection marks; the resulting crossover (≈2029) matches the Bureau’s stated milestone.

The Bureau’s Vintage 2024 release describes the gap as narrowing from “just over 20 million” in 2020 to “just below 12 million” in 2024, using its internally consistent estimates series (whose 2020 figure is based on a mid-year estimate). This page plots the 2020 census count for that year (55.8 million aged 65+, 73.1 million under 18 → a gap of about 17 million), which differs slightly from the estimates-series figure because of the reference date and vintage. The direction and the 2024 endpoint are identical.

Replication. Frequently Asked Questions

When will older adults outnumber children in the U.S.?

Around 2029, according to the Census Bureau’s 2023 National Population Projections (middle series) — the first time in U.S. history. An earlier projection from 2017 put the crossover at 2034, but it has been superseded. As of 2024, children still outnumber older adults nationally (73.1 million versus 61.2 million), though eleven states and nearly half of U.S. counties have already crossed the line.

Why did the projected date move from 2034 to 2029?

The 2017 projection used pre-2020-census, pre-pandemic assumptions. The 2023 projection — the first built on the 2020 census — incorporates lower projected fertility, which pulls the under-18 line down faster and brings the crossover forward by about five years. The observed pace of the gap closing (about 17 million in 2020 to about 12 million in 2024) is consistent with the earlier date.

Is the working-age population shrinking?

Not in absolute terms through 2060 in the middle series — it grows slowly. What declines is the ratio of working-age adults (18–64) to older adults, from about 3.4 today toward roughly 2.4 by 2060. The change is in the balance between groups, not a contraction of the workforce itself.

Is the United States unusually old?

No. In 2020 the U.S. ranked 34th among countries by the share of residents aged 65 and over (16.8%), well behind Japan (28.5%) and much of Europe. The U.S. is aging later and more slowly than most other high-income countries, all of which already have older age structures and remain prosperous economies.

What is driving the shift?

Three long-running forces: the baby-boom generation (born 1946–1964) moving into the 65-plus brackets, with all of them projected to be 65 or older by 2030; rising life expectancy at older ages; and fertility running below the replacement rate of about 2.1 children per woman (around 1.6 recently), which holds the number of children down.

Does this mean the U.S. population will start shrinking?

No. The total population is projected to keep growing for decades, peaking near 370 million around 2080 in the middle series before edging down. The crossover changes the age structure of the population, not its overall size.

Conclusion

For as long as the United States has counted itself, children have outnumbered older adults. On the Census Bureau’s current projections, that ends around 2029. The change has been building for three-quarters of a century — an older population rising five-fold since 1950 while the number of children held roughly flat — and it is already a reality in eleven states and nearly half of U.S. counties. The national crossover is the point at which the rest of the country catches up.

What the data establishes is the timing and the structure of the shift, not its meaning. The same chart reads as a fiscal pressure to some and as a marker of longer lives to others, and the United States enters this transition younger and later than most of its high-income peers. This page is a description of where the age structure is heading, not a prediction of its consequences.

On the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2023 projections (middle series), older adults overtake children around 2029 — the first such crossover in U.S. history, and earlier than the 2034 date in the Bureau’s superseded 2017 projections. Eleven states and nearly half of all U.S. counties have already crossed that line.

blocks.html_en: The two lines on the chart move for different reasons. The number of older Americans has risen almost without interruption: from 12.3 million in 1950 to 16.7 million in 1960, 25.5 million in 1980, 40.3 million in 2010, and 61.2 million by 2024. As a share of the population, the 65-and-older group grew from 8.1% in 1950 to 18.0% in 2024. The single fastest decade was 2010 to 2020, when the older population grew 38.6% — the fastest rate the Census Bureau records since the 1880s — as the first members of the baby-boom generation (born 1946–1964) began turning 65 in 2011.

blocks.html_en: The number of children has followed a flatter, wavier path. It climbed during the baby boom to about 69.8 million in 1970, dipped through the 1980s, recovered to about 74.2 million by 2010 — around its peak — and has since edged down to 73.1 million in 2024. But because the total population kept growing, the share of children declined over the long run — from a baby-boom peak of 36.0% in 1960 to 21.5% in 2024 (it was 31.3% in 1950, before the boom). The result is the long narrowing visible in the chart: a gap approaching 50 million in favour of children around 1970, down to about 12 million by 2024.

blocks.html_en: Between the 2020 census and the 2024 estimate, the mechanics are stark: the number of older adults rose from 55.8 million to 61.2 million — an increase of 5.4 million — while the number of children held essentially flat near 73 million. The entire closing of the gap over those four years came from the top line rising, not the bottom line falling.

blocks.html_en: The exact year of the crossover depends on which projection is used, and this is worth stating precisely because the widely-quoted figure has changed. The Census Bureau’s 2017 National Population Projections placed the crossover at 2034. Those projections have since been superseded by the Bureau’s 2023 National Population Projections — the first set built on the 2020 census and incorporating post-pandemic fertility and mortality. In the 2023 middle series, the older population overtakes the younger around 2029, five years earlier than the prior estimate. The shift reflects lower projected fertility pulling the under-18 line down faster than the 2017 series assumed.

blocks.html_en: The bracketing figures make the timing concrete. In the 2023 projection, children still lead in 2025 (about 70.9 million under 18 versus 63.3 million aged 65+). By 2030 the order has reversed (about 71.2 million aged 65+ versus 69.1 million under 18). The lines cross in between — in 2029. The earlier date is also more consistent with what has actually been observed: the gap closed from about 17 million in 2020 to about 12 million in 2024, a pace that points to the end of this decade rather than the middle of the 2030s.

sentences.en: In the 2023 projection, children still lead in 2025 (about 70.9 million under 18 versus 63.3 million aged 65+).
sentences.zh: 根据 2023 年的预测，到 2025 年，儿童仍处于领先地位（18 岁以下儿童约为 7,090 万人，65 岁以上儿童为 6,330 万人）。

sentences.en: By 2030 the order has reversed (about 71.2 million aged 65+ versus 69.1 million under 18).
sentences.zh: 到 2030 年，这一顺序发生了逆转（65 岁以上人口约为 7120 万，18 岁以下人口为 6910 万）。

blocks.html_en: This is not, in fact, a frontier the whole country reaches at once. As of 2024, eleven states and nearly half of all U.S. counties already had more residents aged 65 and older than children under 18. The national crossover near 2029 is the point at which the rest of the country, on aggregate, catches up to where many states and counties already are.

sentences.en: This is not, in fact, a frontier the whole country reaches at once.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这并不是整个国家一次性达到的边界。

sentences.en: As of 2024, eleven states and nearly half of all U.S. counties already had more residents aged 65 and older than children under 18.

sentences.en: The national crossover near 2029 is the point at which the rest of the country, on aggregate, catches up to where many states and counties already are.
sentences.zh: 到 2029 年左右，全国其他地区总体上将赶上许多州和县的水平。

blocks.html_en: Three forces drive the convergence, and none of them is sudden. The baby-boom cohort is moving through the older age brackets in a single wave — every member of that generation is projected to be 65 or older by 2030. Life expectancy at older ages has risen over the long run, so each cohort lingers longer in the 65-plus group. And fertility has run below the replacement rate of about 2.1 children per woman for years (around 1.6 recently), which holds the under-18 line down. Looking further out, the Bureau’s middle series puts the 65-and-older share at 24.4% by 2060 and 29.1% by 2100, against 17.7% and 16.4% for children.

sentences.en: Three forces drive the convergence, and none of them is sudden.

sentences.en: The baby-boom cohort is moving through the older age brackets in a single wave — every member of that generation is projected to be 65 or older by 2030.
sentences.zh: 婴儿潮一代正在一次性进入老年阶段——预计到 2030 年，这一代人的每个成员都将年满 65 岁或以上。

sentences.en: Life expectancy at older ages has risen over the long run, so each cohort lingers longer in the 65-plus group.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，老年人的预期寿命有所延长，因此 65 岁以上人群中每个群体的寿命都更长。

sentences.zh: 多年来，生育率一直低于每名女性约 2.1 个孩子的替代率（最近约为 1.6 个），这导致 18 岁以下儿童的生育率下降。

blocks.html_en: Two ways to read the same chart

sentences.en: Two ways to read the same chart
sentences.zh: 阅读同一张图表的两种方法

blocks.html_en: The crossover is a single demographic fact, but it supports more than one interpretation, and the data does not settle which is right.

sentences.en: The crossover is a single demographic fact, but it supports more than one interpretation, and the data does not settle which is right.
sentences.zh: 交叉是一个单一的人口统计事实，但它支持不止一种解释，而且数据并不能确定哪种解释是正确的。

blocks.html_en: Some read this as a slow-moving fiscal pressure. Programs for older Americans — Social Security and Medicare in particular — are funded largely by working-age contributions. As the ratio of working-age adults (18–64) to older adults falls from about 3.4 today toward roughly 2.4 by 2060, the arithmetic that supports those programs tightens, all else equal. On this reading, the chart is an argument for some combination of higher productivity, longer working lives, higher fertility, or higher immigration to widen the working-age base.

sentences.en: Some read this as a slow-moving fiscal pressure.
sentences.zh: 一些人将此视为缓慢的财政压力。

sentences.en: Programs for older Americans — Social Security and Medicare in particular — are funded largely by working-age contributions.
sentences.zh: 针对美国老年人的计划——特别是社会保障和医疗保险——主要由工作年龄缴款提供资金。

sentences.en: As the ratio of working-age adults (18–64) to older adults falls from about 3.4 today toward roughly 2.4 by 2060, the arithmetic that supports those programs tightens, all else equal.
sentences.zh: 随着工作年龄成年人（18-64 岁）与老年人的比例从现在的 3.4 左右下降到 2060 年的 2.4 左右，在其他条件相同的情况下，支持这些计划的算术将更加严格。

sentences.en: On this reading, the chart is an argument for some combination of higher productivity, longer working lives, higher fertility, or higher immigration to widen the working-age base.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，该图表论证了将更高的生产率、更长的工作寿命、更高的生育率或更高的移民结合起来以扩大工作年龄基础。

blocks.html_en: Others read this as a marker of success rather than a problem. A growing older population is, in large part, the result of people living longer — a public-health achievement, not a failure. On this reading, the United States is also far from an outlier: in 2020 it ranked 34th among countries by the share of residents aged 65 and over, behind Japan (28.5%) and much of Europe, all of which remain high-income economies. The U.S. is aging later and more slowly than most of its peers, and an older age structure is something many wealthy societies already manage.

sentences.en: Others read this as a marker of success rather than a problem.
sentences.zh: 其他人将此视为成功的标志而不是问题。

sentences.en: A growing older population is, in large part, the result of people living longer — a public-health achievement, not a failure.
sentences.zh: 人口老龄化在很大程度上是人们寿命延长的结果——这是公共卫生成就，而不是失败。

sentences.en: On this reading, the United States is also far from an outlier: in 2020 it ranked 34th among countries by the share of residents aged 65 and over, behind Japan (28.5%) and much of Europe, all of which remain high-income economies.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，美国也远非异常：2020 年，美国 65 岁及以上居民比例在各国中排名第 34 位，落后于日本（28.5%）和欧洲大部分国家，而这些国家仍然是高收入经济体。

sentences.en: The U.S. is aging later and more slowly than most of its peers, and an older age structure is something many wealthy societies already manage.
sentences.zh: 与大多数其他国家相比，美国的老龄化较晚且较慢，而且许多富裕社会已经在应对老龄化结构。

blocks.html_en: The chart shows the when and the structure of the shift. It does not show which policy response is correct, or whether the trajectory is a concern at all — that depends on assumptions the data alone cannot supply. Is the U.S. path more like Japan’s — older, slower-growing, and still high-income — or a manageable mid-century adjustment? The same chart is read both ways.

sentences.en: The chart shows the when and the structure of the shift.
sentences.zh: 该图表显示了轮班的时间和结构。

sentences.en: It does not show which policy response is correct, or whether the trajectory is a concern at all — that depends on assumptions the data alone cannot supply.
sentences.zh: 它没有表明哪种政策反应是正确的，也没有表明轨迹是否值得关注——这取决于数据本身无法提供的假设。

sentences.en: Is the U.S. path more like Japan’s — older, slower-growing, and still high-income — or a manageable mid-century adjustment?
sentences.zh: 美国的道路是否更像日本的道路——历史悠久、增长缓慢且仍然是高收入国家——还是可控的本世纪中叶调整？

sentences.en: The same chart is read both ways.
sentences.zh: 同一张图表可以用两种方式读取。

blocks.html_en: Counter-arguments and limitations

sentences.en: Counter-arguments and limitations
sentences.zh: 反驳和限制

blocks.html_en: The crossover year is a projection, not an observation. Children still outnumber older adults today. The 2029 date comes from the Census Bureau’s 2023 middle series, one of several scenarios. Higher immigration would widen the working-age and child base and could push the crossover later; lower immigration or fertility would pull it earlier. The Bureau itself publishes high-, low-, and zero-immigration variants alongside the middle series for exactly this reason.

sentences.en: The crossover year is a projection, not an observation.
sentences.zh: 交叉年是一个预测，而不是一个观察。

sentences.en: Children still outnumber older adults today.
sentences.zh: 如今，儿童数量仍然多于老年人。

sentences.en: The 2029 date comes from the Census Bureau’s 2023 middle series, one of several scenarios.
sentences.zh: 2029 年日期来自人口普查局 2023 年中间系列，是几种情景之一。

sentences.en: Higher immigration would widen the working-age and child base and could push the crossover later; lower immigration or fertility would pull it earlier.
sentences.zh: 增加移民将扩大工作年龄和儿童基础，并可能推动稍后的交叉；较低的移民或生育率会将其拉得更早。

sentences.en: The Bureau itself publishes high-, low-, and zero-immigration variants alongside the middle series for exactly this reason.
sentences.zh: 正是出于这个原因，该局本身在中间系列的同时发布了高、低和零移民变体。

blocks.html_en: Counts and shares can tell slightly different stories. This page plots counts in millions, because the milestone — “more older adults than children” — is a statement about numbers of people. The crossover appears at the same point if the two groups are measured as a share of the population, since they share the same denominator. But share-based and count-based framings of “how much the country is aging” can diverge, and both are included in the downloadable dataset.

sentences.en: Counts and shares can tell slightly different stories.
sentences.zh: 计数和份额可以讲述略有不同的故事。

sentences.en: This page plots counts in millions, because the milestone — “more older adults than children” — is a statement about numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 此页面的绘图以百万为单位，因为里程碑——“老年人多于儿童”——是关于人数的陈述。

sentences.en: The crossover appears at the same point if the two groups are measured as a share of the population, since they share the same denominator.
sentences.zh: 如果将两个群体作为人口的一部分来衡量，那么交叉会出现在同一点，因为它们具有相同的分母。

sentences.en: But share-based and count-based framings of “how much the country is aging” can diverge, and both are included in the downloadable dataset.
sentences.zh: 但基于份额和基于计数的“国家老龄化程度”框架可能会有所不同，并且两者都包含在可下载的数据集中。

blocks.html_en: Age thresholds are conventions. “65 and older” and “under 18” are administratively meaningful (retirement eligibility, school age) but arbitrary as biological or economic categories. A 67-year-old in the labour force and a 17-year-old earner sit on the “wrong” side of those lines. The crossover is robust to small changes in the thresholds, but the precise gap is sensitive to where they are drawn.

sentences.en: Age thresholds are conventions.
sentences.zh: 年龄阈值是惯例。

sentences.en: “65 and older” and “under 18” are administratively meaningful (retirement eligibility, school age) but arbitrary as biological or economic categories.
sentences.zh: “65 岁及以上”和“18 岁以下”在行政上是有意义的（退休资格、学龄），但作为生物或经济类别是任意的。

sentences.en: A 67-year-old in the labour force and a 17-year-old earner sit on the “wrong” side of those lines.
sentences.zh: 一名 67 岁的劳动力和一名 17 岁的工薪阶层则处于“错误”的一方。

sentences.en: The crossover is robust to small changes in the thresholds, but the precise gap is sensitive to where they are drawn.
sentences.zh: 交叉对阈值的微小变化具有鲁棒性，但精确的间隙对其绘制位置敏感。

blocks.html_en: The drivers are not equally certain. The baby-boom cohort’s path through the older brackets is close to fixed — those people are already alive and counted. Future fertility and immigration are far less predictable, and they are what determine how far past the crossover the gap eventually widens.

sentences.en: The drivers are not equally certain.
sentences.zh: 司机们并不同样确定。

sentences.en: The baby-boom cohort’s path through the older brackets is close to fixed — those people are already alive and counted.
sentences.zh: 婴儿潮一代穿过较老群体的路径几乎是固定的——这些人已经活着并且被计算在内。

sentences.en: Future fertility and immigration are far less predictable, and they are what determine how far past the crossover the gap eventually widens.
sentences.zh: 未来的生育率和移民更难以预测，而它们决定了交叉之后差距最终会扩大多远。

blocks.html_en: Common misinterpretations

sentences.en: Common misinterpretations
sentences.zh: 常见的误解

blocks.html_en: Reading the crossover as already having happened nationally. It has not. As of the 2024 estimate, children still outnumber older adults in the country as a whole (73.1 million versus 61.2 million). The crossover is projected, not realised — even though it has already occurred in eleven states and nearly half of U.S. counties.

sentences.en: Reading the crossover as already having happened nationally.
sentences.zh: 将跨界解读为已经在全国范围内发生。

sentences.en: It has not.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: As of the 2024 estimate, children still outnumber older adults in the country as a whole (73.1 million versus 61.2 million).
sentences.zh: 截至 2024 年估计，全国儿童人数仍多于老年人（7,310 万对 6,120 万）。

sentences.en: The crossover is projected, not realised — even though it has already occurred in eleven states and nearly half of U.S. counties.
sentences.zh: 尽管这种交叉已经在美国十一个州和近一半的县发生，但这种交叉是预计的，而不是实现的。

blocks.html_en: Treating 2029 and 2034 as competing facts. They are not contradictory; 2034 is simply the older estimate. The 2017 projections placed the crossover at 2034; the 2023 projections, which supersede them, place it at 2029. Citing 2034 today means citing a figure the Bureau has replaced.

content_html_zh:
在美国历史上的大部分时间里，儿童的数量远远超过老年人。 美国人口普查局现在预测，这种情况将在 2029 年左右发生逆转，届时 65 岁及以上的美国人将首次超过 18 岁以下的儿童。

这种转变并不是对遥远世纪的预测。 1950 年，几乎每个老年人对应四个孩子。 到 2024 年，这两个群体的人口差距约为 1200 万，并且正在接近。 最新的官方预测将交叉时间定在本十年末。 本页面使用该局自己的统计和预测记录了收敛情况，并提供完整的数据集可供下载。

TL;DR — 自 1950 年以来，美国 65 岁以上成年人的数量大约增加了五倍（1230 万至 6120 万），而 18 岁以下儿童的数量一直保持在 7300 万左右。 根据美国人口普查局 2023 年的预测（中间系列），老年人在 2029 年左右超过儿童，这是美国历史上的首次此类交叉，并且早于人口普查局取代的 2017 年预测中的 2034 年日期。 十一个州和美国近一半的县已经跨越了这条线。

图表上的两条线由于不同的原因而移动。 美国老年人的数量几乎不间断地增长：从1950年的1230万增加到1960年的1670万，1980年的2550万，2010年的4030万，到2024年的6120万。 65岁及以上群体占总人口的比例从1950年的8.1%增长到2024年的18.0%。 最快的十年是 2010 年至 2020 年，随着婴儿潮一代（出生于 1946 年至 1964 年）的第一批成员于 2011 年开始年满 65 岁，老年人口增长了 38.6%（人口普查局记录的自 1880 年代以来的最快增长率）。

儿童数量呈现出更加平坦、波动的趋势。 该数字在 1970 年婴儿潮期间攀升至约 6,980 万，在 1980 年代有所下降，到 2010 年恢复至约 7,420 万（接近峰值），此后在 2024 年微降至 7,310 万。 但由于总人口持续增长，从长远来看，儿童比例有所下降——从 1960 年婴儿潮高峰时期的 36.0% 下降到 2024 年的 21.5%（婴儿潮爆发前的 1950 年为 31.3%）。 结果是图表中可见的长期缩小：1970 年左右，儿童的差距接近 5000 万，到 2024 年下降到约 1200 万。

在 2020 年人口普查和 2024 年估计之间，情况很明显：老年人数量从 5580 万增加到 6120 万，增加了 540 万，而儿童数量基本持平，接近 7300 万。 这四年间差距的缩小完全来自于营收的上升，而不是净利润的下降。

交叉以及日期移动的原因

交叉的确切年份取决于使用的投影，这一点值得准确说明，因为广泛引用的数字已经发生了变化。 人口普查局 2017 年全国人口预测将交叉点定为 2034 年。 这些预测后来被该局的 2023 年全国人口预测所取代，这是第一套基于 2020 年人口普查的预测，纳入了大流行后的生育率和死亡率。 在 2023 年中期数据中，老年人口在 2029 年左右超过年轻人口，比之前的估计提前了五年。 这一转变反映出预计生育率下降导致 18 岁以下儿童生育率下降速度快于 2017 年系列的假设。

包围数字使时间变得具体。 根据 2023 年的预测，到 2025 年，儿童仍处于领先地位（18 岁以下儿童约为 7,090 万人，65 岁以上儿童为 6,330 万人）。 到 2030 年，这一顺序发生了逆转（65 岁以上人口约为 7120 万，18 岁以下人口为 6910 万）。 两条线在 2029 年交叉。 较早的日期也更符合实际观察到的情况：这一差距从 2020 年的约 1700 万缩小到 2024 年的约 1200 万，这一速度表明本世纪末，而不是 2030 年代中期。

事实上，这并不是整个国家一次性达到的边界。 截至 2024 年，美国 11 个州和近一半县的 65 岁及以上居民数量已超过 18 岁以下儿童。 到 2029 年左右，全国其他地区总体上将赶上许多州和县的水平。

三种力量推动着这种融合，而且没有一种力量是突然的。 婴儿潮一代正在一次性进入老年阶段——预计到 2030 年，这一代人的每个成员都将年满 65 岁或以上。 从长远来看，老年人的预期寿命有所延长，因此 65 岁以上人群中每个群体的寿命都更长。 多年来，生育率一直低于每名女性约 2.1 个孩子的替代率（最近约为 1.6 个），这导致 18 岁以下儿童的生育率下降。 展望未来，该局的中间数据显示，到 2060 年，65 岁及以上老年人的比例将达到 24.4%，到 2100 年将达到 29.1%，而儿童的比例为 17.7% 和 16.4%。

阅读同一张图表的两种方法

交叉是一个单一的人口统计事实，但它支持不止一种解释，而且数据并不能确定哪种解释是正确的。

一些人将此视为缓慢的财政压力。 针对美国老年人的计划——特别是社会保障和医疗保险——主要由工作年龄缴款提供资金。 随着工作年龄成年人（18-64 岁）与老年人的比例从现在的 3.4 左右下降到 2060 年的 2.4 左右，在其他条件相同的情况下，支持这些计划的算术将更加严格。 从这个角度来看，该图表论证了将更高的生产率、更长的工作寿命、更高的生育率或更高的移民结合起来以扩大工作年龄基础。

其他人将此视为成功的标志而不是问题。 人口老龄化在很大程度上是人们寿命延长的结果——这是公共卫生成就，而不是失败。 从这个角度来看，美国也远非异常：2020 年，美国 65 岁及以上居民比例在各国中排名第 34 位，落后于日本（28.5%）和欧洲大部分国家，而这些国家仍然是高收入经济体。 与大多数其他国家相比，美国的老龄化较晚且较慢，而且许多富裕社会已经在应对老龄化结构。

该图表显示了轮班的时间和结构。 它没有表明哪种政策反应是正确的，也没有表明轨迹是否值得关注——这取决于数据本身无法提供的假设。 美国的道路是否更像日本的道路——历史悠久、增长缓慢且仍然是高收入国家——还是可控的本世纪中叶调整？ 同一张图表可以用两种方式读取。

反驳和限制

交叉年是一个预测，而不是一个观察。 如今，儿童数量仍然多于老年人。 2029 年日期来自人口普查局 2023 年中间系列，是几种情景之一。 增加移民将扩大工作年龄和儿童基础，并可能推动稍后的交叉；较低的移民或生育率会将其拉得更早。 正是出于这个原因，该局本身在中间系列的同时发布了高、低和零移民变体。

计数和份额可以讲述略有不同的故事。 此页面的绘图以百万为单位，因为里程碑——“老年人多于儿童”——是关于人数的陈述。 如果将两个群体作为人口的一部分来衡量，那么交叉会出现在同一点，因为它们具有相同的分母。 但基于份额和基于计数的“国家老龄化程度”框架可能会有所不同，并且两者都包含在可下载的数据集中。

年龄阈值是惯例。 “65 岁及以上”和“18 岁以下”在行政上是有意义的（退休资格、学龄），但作为生物或经济类别是任意的。 一名 67 岁的劳动力和一名 17 岁的工薪阶层则处于“错误”的一方。 交叉对阈值的微小变化具有鲁棒性，但精确的间隙对其绘制位置敏感。

司机们并不同样确定。 婴儿潮一代穿过较老群体的路径几乎是固定的——这些人已经活着并且被计算在内。 未来的生育率和移民更难以预测，而它们决定了交叉之后差距最终会扩大多远。

常见的误解

将跨界解读为已经在全国范围内发生。 但事实并非如此。 截至 2024 年估计，全国儿童人数仍多于老年人（7,310 万对 6,120 万）。 尽管这种交叉已经在美国十一个州和近一半的县发生，但这种交叉是预计的，而不是实现的。

将 2029 年和 2034 年视为相互竞争的事实。 它们并不矛盾； 2034 年只是较旧的估计。 2017 年的预测将交叉点定为 2034 年；取代它们的 2023 年预测将其定为 2029 年。 今天引用 2034 意味着引用无线电通信局已替换的数字。

将“老年人增多”等同于“工作年龄人口减少”。 预计到 2050 年代，工作年龄人口（18-64 岁）将继续增长，然后在中期保持大致水平，而不是收缩。 下降的是工作年龄成年人与老年人的比例。 这种压力是相对的，而不是劳动力的实际收缩。

阅读图表作为下降的预测。 美国总人口预计将持续增长数十年，在中期数据中的 2080 年左右达到峰值，接近 3.7 亿。 交叉是人口年龄结构的变化，而不是人口规模的变化。

常见问题解答

美国老年人的数量何时会超过儿童？

根据人口普查局的 2023 年全国人口预测（中间系列），2029 年左右，这在美国历史上尚属首次。 2017 年的早期预测将交叉点定为 2034 年，但已被取代。 截至 2024 年，全国儿童数量仍然超过老年人（7310 万对 6120 万），尽管美国有 11 个州和近一半的县已经超过了这一界限。

为什么预计日期从 2034 年移至 2029 年？

2017 年的预测使用了 2020 年人口普查前、大流行前的假设。 2023 年的预测——首次建立在 2020 年人口普查的基础上——包含了较低的预测生育率，这使得 18 岁以下人口线下降得更快，并使交叉提前了大约五年。 观察到的差距缩小速度（2020 年约 1700 万至 2024 年约 1200 万）与之前的日期一致。

劳动年龄人口正在减少吗？

在中期系列中，从绝对值来看，到 2060 年，增长缓慢。 下降的是工作年龄成年人（18-64 岁）与老年人的比例，从现在的约 3.4 下降到 2060 年的约 2.4。 这种变化在于群体之间的平衡，而不是劳动力本身的收缩。

美国是不是异常古老？

不会。2020 年，美国 65 岁及以上居民比例（16.8%）在各国中排名第 34 位，远远落后于日本（28.5%）和欧洲大部分国家。 与大多数其他高收入国家相比，美国的老龄化较晚且较慢，所有这些国家都已经出现老龄化结构，并且经济仍然繁荣。

是什么推动了这种转变？

三个长期存在的力量：婴儿潮一代（1946-1964 年出生）进入 65 岁以上年龄段，预计到 2030 年他们都将达到 65 岁或以上；老年人预期寿命延长；生育率低于每名妇女约 2.1 个孩子的更替率（最近约为 1.6 个），这抑制了孩子的数量。

这是否意味着美国人口将开始减少？

不会。总人口预计将持续增长数十年，在中期数据中于 2080 年左右达到接近 3.7 亿的峰值，然后逐渐下降。 交叉改变了人口的年龄结构，而不是总体规模。

结论

自美国统计以来，儿童的数量就超过了老年人的数量。 根据人口普查局目前的预测，这一情况将于 2029 年左右结束。 这种变化已经持续了四分之三个世纪——自 1950 年以来，老年人口数量增加了五倍，而儿童数量基本持平——而且这种变化已经在美国 11 个州和近一半的县成为现实。 全国交叉点是该国其他地区迎头赶上的点。

数据确定的是转变的时间和结构，而不是其含义。 同一张图表对某些人来说是财政压力，对另一些人来说则是寿命延长的标志，而美国比大多数高收入国家更早、更晚地进入这一转变。 本页描述了年龄结构的发展方向，而不是对其后果的预测。
